messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The standard deviation (standard error) of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis is:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx 0.22
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis. The standard error is sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That is indeed the standard error: sigma / sqrt(n). They gave sample_std_dev=1.4, sample_size=40. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = about 0.2215. But they also mention population mean of 98.6. That might be used for t-test calculation. But the question: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6." They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. That is the standard error of the mean: 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.2215.

But we have a tool: statistics_calculate_p_value. That calculates p-value for a t-test. But the user didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. We can compute it manually. There's no tool for that. So we just compute it ourselves. The standard deviation of the null hypothesis test is the standard error: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). So answer: approximately 0.2215.
